title: Gerry Wimmer Pitches Caldwell Partners $CWL.TO at Planet MicroCap Toronto 2026

summary: The speaker argues that Caldwell Partners is an undervalued, undiscovered microcap opportunity with a simple revenue model and a definable growth strategy led by CEO Chris Beck. The company operates in the elite quadrant of the executive search market, generating growing revenues and profits that outpace operating expenses to demonstrate significant operating leverage. With a strong balance sheet featuring $14 million in cash and zero debt, the firm offers capital allocation optionality, an attractive valuation, and a generous dividend yield of over 5.5%.

claims.claim: The speaker pitches Caldwell Partners as an undervalued, undiscovered microcap with a simple revenue model, growing revenues and profits, strong balance sheet, and significant capital allocation optionality.
claims.quote: My pick today is a company that doesn't get a lot of exposure. Symbol CWL on the Toronto Stock Exchange. That's Caldwell Partners International. So, why am I pitching Caldwell to you here today? For five reasons. Definitely undiscovered and in my opinion, undervalued.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker highlights Caldwell's growth strategy led by CEO Chris Beck, noting that revenues and profits are currently growing alongside a definable growth strategy.
claims.quote: Today, the company's revenues and profits are growing. The CEO of Caldwell is leading a very definable growth strategy. And also, there's lots of capital allocation optionality at this company.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Caldwell operates in the elite quadrant of the executive search market, placing high-level executives, and possesses a unique market position compared to boutique firms.
claims.quote: I like putting this chart up because it shows Caldwell's unique market position. And why I say it's unique is that Caldwell operates in the elite quadrum of executive search market.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker points out that Caldwell's trailing 12-month revenue growth is greater than its OpEx growth, resulting in higher operating and net income, demonstrating operating leverage.
claims.quote: So, if you look at the trailing 12-month revenue growth, it's greater than its OpEx growth and equates to a higher operating and net income.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker views Caldwell Partners as an attractive investment due to its scale, operating leverage, strong balance sheet, and attractive valuation.
claims.quote: Caldwell is of scale now, over 100 million of revenues, and the operating leverage is showing. So, if you look at the trailing 12-month revenue growth, it's greater than its OpEx growth and equates to a higher operating and net income.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker finds the company attractive as of October 15th, noting a market cap of 31 million and inexpensive valuation ratios compared to peers.
claims.quote: For the stock evaluation, I said it I find that the company is attractive as of October 15th, the stock price is a little higher today, um with a market cap of 31 million, the valuation ratios are very inexpensive for micro cap stock compared to other ones, and obviously within its peer group.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker highlights the strong balance sheet with $14 million cash and zero bank debt, providing capital allocation optionality for growth.
claims.quote: I do want to point out that cash on hand is $14 million and a zero bank debt, so the company has a very very balance sheet. I do also want to point out that outstanding shares at 29.5 million. That was of May 30th. That share count has dropped now to 28 million due to cancellations that have occurred since.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer

claims.claim: The speaker believes the stock is undiscovered with no analyst coverage, attractive valuation, and offers a generous dividend yield of over 5.5%.
claims.quote: The stock is undiscovered. I'm probably the only one that talks about it. Doesn't have any analyst coverage. They're not raising any capital. Stock valuation is attractive given some some of the valuation metrics I pointed out. Also the strong balance sheet provides a lot of capital allocation optionality and flexibility. And finally, if you buy the stock, you'll earn a very generous payout, dividend payout, with a yield of over 5.5% to hold it and enjoy some of the equity gains along the way.
claims.speaker: Gerry Wimmer
